speaker: freelancer
text: Am I correct that this board contains the esp32, ina219, usb, connectors, and their related components?

speaker: client
text:
Correct. Sensors and power-management circuitry stay on the other boards; the main board contains:

\- ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module
\- INA219 current monitor measuring the 3.3V rail
\- USB-C programming connector plus an LDO for standalone operation
\- All JST connectors for the power board, sensor board, display, PIR, touch inputs, LEDs, buttons, and reset
\- Supporting components including decoupling capacitors, pull-ups, series resistors, Schottky diodes, and a BOOT button

speaker: client
text:
Here is the complete mapping:

\- The J\_BTN3 panel button is assigned to GPIO6
\- The J\_BTN4 panel button is assigned to GPIO7
\- The J\_SW panel slide switch is assigned to GPIO8
\- The J\_RESET panel reset button connects EN to GND
\- The J\_TOUCH capacitive-touch connector uses TTP223 and is assigned to GPIO11
\- The J\_TOUCH2 capacitive-touch connector uses TTP223 and is assigned to GPIO14
\- The BOOT button is on-board only for development and is not panel-mounted

speaker: freelancer
text: Am I right in counting 14 connectors in total on the board?

speaker: client
text: The count is 14 JST connectors, with an additional on-board USB-C; most have low pin counts.

speaker: client
text: By low pins, I was referring to every connector except the interboard ones.

speaker: client
text: The power board is no problem, so could you instead add a 2-pin JST-GH connector to the main board for a panel-mounted power button? PWRON already arrives through J\_PWR\_SIG pin 4; the new connector only needs to tap that line so a button can be wired from the enclosure panel.

speaker: freelancer
text: For the sensor board connectors, I'm uncertain: are power and sensor signal the only ones coming from the main board?

speaker: client
text: From the main board, only these two connections go to the sensor board: J\_SENSOR\_PWR, using a 4-pin JST-PH at 2.0mm, and J\_SENSOR\_SIG, using a 6-pin JST-GH at 1.25mm.

speaker: freelancer
text: Can you provide the connector locations for both the Main board and the Sensor board?

speaker: freelancer
text: Within the supplied main-board dimensions, fitting everything is not possible.

speaker: client
text: Because the main and sensor boards slide vertically into the enclosure rails, each is mounted with its long edge at the top. Put the high-pin-count main connectors along that long top edge on both boards, with none on either side or the bottom. On the main board, J\_SENSOR\_PWR and J\_SENSOR\_SIG must line up with J\_SENSOR\_PWR and J\_SENSOR\_SIG on the sensor board at the same relative locations along the top edge; this keeps the inter-board cables short and lets them run straight between the boards.

speaker: client
text: Since this is a prototype, the dimensions and similar details can change. In the layout, the small sensor board is on the left, the main board is in the middle, and the power board is on the right. The important point is that they stand vertically: cables will be easier to connect from the top, while smaller connectors can go on the sides.
